method: Reviewed the complete lesson, metadata, existing historical-claim boundary, runnable environment model, teardown negative control, and current official OpenAI evaluation and pytest fixture documentation. Reproduced the catch-all exception-classification defect with a failing boundary probe before editing, then ran the W6 verifier and both complete lesson Python fences under Python 3.14.7. No model, provider, or external service calls.

observations.trace: The previous runner caught every Exception as system_error, obscuring whether fixture, agent execution, environment/tool, grader, or cleanup failed. A pre-fix probe expected agent_runtime_error but observed system_error. The updated runner reports invalid_fixture, environment_error, agent_runtime_error, grader_error, and scored as separate primary outcomes, while attaching cleanup status independently so cleanup failure does not replace the execution result. W6 fault-injection assertions pass for all categories; the negative teardown example still reproduces its expected AssertionError. The historical 2026-10-09 3/5 claim remains withdrawn because raw request, tool-return, and scorer records are missing.
observations.screenshotDimensions: 1280x11326 in light and dark themes; full-page visual inspection

limitations: The teaching environment uses an in-memory dictionary. It does not establish database, filesystem, container, sandbox, third-party service, cleanup, concurrency, or production isolation behavior.
No live model/provider run or stochastic-repeat analysis was performed, and the historical 3/5 result cannot be reconstructed.
The exception categories require production adapters to classify failures at their actual boundaries; an untyped exception cannot identify its root cause by itself.
